content.text: No audit, inspection, verification, or system-access right running against Clear Capital exists anywhere in the agreement (§§ 1, 3, 4 and the searches for audit/inspection/records/compliance-monitoring all come back empty).

input.quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
input.rationale: The agreement grants RadialSpark no audit, inspection, verification or usage-review right against Clear Capital. Compensation is time-and-materials, verified through Contractor's own invoices and supporting detail (§ 3(b)), and the only access provisions run the other way — Contractor's personnel must comply with Company's security and system-access policies when at a Company facility (§ 1(c)). Searches for audit, inspection, records, verification, compliance monitoring and system access return nothing, and §§ 1, 3 and 4 contain no such right. Because there is no Vendor audit right to constrain, the AUDIT rule's frequency, notice, off-site, auditor-independence, cost-allocation and no-system-access limits are unnecessary; the absence of any audit right is more protective than either the preferred or fallback position. We therefore do not propose inserting audit machinery against ourselves.
